prompt: Implement sc_witness(threads, modification_order) for a fixed straight-line C++20 all-seq_cst atomic load/store model. Each distinct modeled object is a valid disjoint atomic unsigned integer initialized to0 before all threads start; every real store writes1. There are no other modifications, RMWs, fences, consume operations, ordinary shared accesses, data-dependent branches or lifetime violations. threads is a dictionary of0..6 thread IDs to lists of0..6 operations, with at most20 operations total. Each list defines that thread's program order; dictionary iteration order creates NO cross-thread order. A store is exactly {id:str,object:str,kind:'store'}; a load is exactly {id:str,object:str,kind:'load',reads_from:None_or_store_id}. Every operation ID is globally unique. Thread/object/operation identifiers are case-sensitive1..32-character ASCII [A-Za-z0-9_-] strings. modification_order maps0..4 object IDs to lists containing all and only that object's real store IDs, exactly once, in their proposed modification order. Every used object is present; unused objects with an empty store list are allowed. A non-None reads_from names a store of the same object; None names the initial zero write. The source ID is supplied execution-witness information, not inferred from equal stored values. All stores write the same1, so different matching values do not erase their distinct identities. Inputs are structurally valid, but the proposed orders/RF choices may be jointly inconsistent. Return None when no sequentially consistent order exists; otherwise return the lexicographically smallest list of ALL real operation IDs forming a valid order. It must preserve each thread's full program order across objects, preserve each supplied per-object store order, and make every load observe its exact MOST RECENT preceding store on that object (or the initial value when no real store precedes it). Initial writes are not returned as operation IDs. Empty execution returns[]. Lexicographic order is ordinary case-sensitive Python string ordering. None rejects this candidate witness within the stated model; it does not mean that the whole source program has undefined behavior. No outside-domain validation is required. Inputs must remain unchanged and calls independent. Standard library only; the task is an exact bounded ordering analysis, not a compiler or a complete weak-memory execution validator. All input/output containers in this task are built-in Python dict/list values; tuples and custom container classes are outside this exact interface.

Implement synchronization_witness(events, modification_orders), a bounded C++20 classifier of direct CROSS-THREAD synchronization witnesses. It does not validate every C++ execution, SC total order, object lifetime or program behavior, and does not return transitive happens-before closure. events has0..24 records over at most4 threads and4 objects; its list order defines ONLY the sequenced-before order of records from the same thread, never cross-thread time or modification order. All IDs are case-sensitive1..24-character ASCII [A-Za-z0-9_-] strings, with globally unique event IDs. Every event has id,thread,kind,order. A store also has object,value; load or cas_fail also has object,reads_from; rmw also has object,value,reads_from; fence has no object/value/reads_from. Integer written values in[-9,9], not bool, are opaque; equal values never identify a read source. Allowed orders: store relaxed/release/seq_cst; load and cas_fail relaxed/acquire/seq_cst; rmw relaxed/acquire/release/acq_rel/seq_cst; fence relaxed/acquire/release/acq_rel/seq_cst. Failed CAS is a read only, not a modification; no expected-argument output is modeled. modification_orders maps every present object to a nonempty list containing exactly its stores and successful RMW IDs once. Every reads_from names an explicit modification of the same object; an RMW reads its immediate modification-order predecessor, so no RMW is first. All supplying modifications are explicit; there is no implicit initial-value event. Empty events and empty map are valid. Return exactly {release_sequences:{head_id:[head,...continuing_RMW_ids]},synchronizes_with:[[source_id,target_id],...]}. Heads are modifications with release/acq_rel/seq_cst semantics; each sequence includes its head then contiguous RMWs until the next plain store, regardless of their threads. A release RMW may extend older sequences while heading its own. Sequence members retain supplied MO order; SW pairs are unique and lexicographically sorted, and only source/target events on DIFFERENT threads are reported. Apply release-atomic to acquire-read synchronization when the read (load, successful RMW or failed CAS with acquire/acq_rel/SC semantics as applicable) reads the release or a member of its sequence. A release fence A can synchronize with an acquire read Y when A is sequenced before carrier modification X and Y reads X or its hypothetical release sequence. A release modification H can synchronize with acquire fence B when read Y reads H or H's release sequence and Y is sequenced before B. Release fence A can synchronize with acquire fence B through modification X and read Y when A is sequenced before X, Y reads X or X's hypothetical release sequence, and Y is sequenced before B. A hypothetical sequence is X followed by contiguous RMWs, as if X were a release head. Release/acquire roles include acq_rel and seq_cst where legal; relaxed fences have neither role. Return only direct qualifying pairs, not SB edges or transitive pairs. All inputs satisfy the listed structural/witness preconditions; no validation outside them is required. Inputs remain unchanged and calls independent; standard library only. All input/output containers in this task are built-in Python dict/list values; tuples and custom container classes are outside this exact interface.

Implement reduce_resources(available, processes) for a declared closed reusable-resource completion model. available is a vector of1..8 nonnegative integers, each<=1000. processes has0..12 exact records {id:str,allocation:[ints],request:[ints]}, with vectors of that same length, entries0..1000, and unique case-sensitive IDs matching ASCII [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}. All integers exclude bool. For each type j, total[j]=available[j]+sum(allocation[p][j]); each process satisfies allocation[p][j]+request[p][j]<=total[j]. request is the CURRENT additional outstanding requirement, not a maximum future Banker claim. There are no arrivals, new requests, preemption, partial grants, timeouts or external releases. A process can complete when its ENTIRE request is componentwise<=current work. Grant that complete request, assume it finishes, and release both its old allocation and new grant; the net work increase is its OLD allocation, not its request. Repeatedly select the lexicographically smallest currently eligible unfinished ID at EVERY iteration until none is eligible. Return exactly {order:[completion_ids],work:[final_available_ints],blocked:[remaining_ids_sorted],deficits:{remaining_id:[max(request[j]-work[j],0),...]}}. blocked includes every process unfinishable under this stated closed completion/release model, including zero-allocation downstream waiters; it is not a minimal deadlock-cycle membership set. Resources may have multiple interchangeable instances, so a cycle between resource TYPES is not by itself the answer. The returned order is the specified canonical possible completion witness, not a real scheduler deadline or fairness guarantee. Deficits has exactly the blocked IDs as keys. Calls are fresh and inputs unchanged; no outside-domain validation required; standard library only. All input/output containers in this task are built-in Python dict/list values; tuples and custom container classes are outside this exact interface.

Implement hazard_trace(nodes, source, events), a declared bounded SC symbolic protocol/lifetime monitor with no actual pointer dereference. nodes contains0..8 unique case-sensitive ASCII IDs matching [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}, all initially live/allocated. source is None or a listed node. events has at most100 entries and at most8 distinct reader IDs of the same syntax. Exact event schemas are {op:'load',reader:id}, {op:'publish',reader:id}, {op:'validate',reader:id}, {op:'clear',reader:id}, {op:'use',reader:id}, {op:'set_source',node:id_or_None}, {op:'retire',node:id}, or {op:'scan'}. First mention of a reader creates {candidate:None,hazard:None,validated:False}. load copies current source to candidate and resets validation, retaining any old hazard. publish copies candidate to hazard and resets validation; publishing a stale freed symbolic ID is allowed but never resurrects it. validate sets the flag to true iff candidate is nonnull, equals BOTH source and hazard, and is not reclaimed. clear clears hazard and validation but retains candidate. set_source replaces source and does not alter readers; its new node must be None or a live, never-retired listed node. retire requires a live, not-current-source, never-retired node and puts it on the retired set. scan is one complete noninterleaved SC observation of ALL hazard slots, even unvalidated ones: reclaim every retired ID absent from all slots, remove it from retired and add it to the permanent reclaimed set. use changes no state and returns the first applicable status: empty if candidate is None; reclaimed if candidate is freed; unprotected if hazard!=candidate; unvalidated if validation is false; otherwise safe. Here safe means satisfying these modeled protocol/lifetime gates, not an iff test of physical memory safety or proof of logical algorithm correctness. A protected validated candidate remains qualified after unlink/retire; source changes alone do not erase validation. All commands obey schema/lifecycle preconditions; no outside-domain validation required. Return a list containing one separate snapshot per event; empty events returns[]. Each snapshot has exact keys {op,result,source,retired,reclaimed,readers}. retired and reclaimed are sorted disjoint ID lists; readers maps each seen reader ID to its three fields. result is the candidate/hazard ID or None for load/publish; Boolean for validate; sorted newly reclaimed IDs for scan; the status string for use; None for clear/set_source/retire. Calls start fresh, input structures and earlier snapshots remain unchanged. Live source A->B->A is permitted and supplies no logical-ABA correctness proof. There is no allocation reuse, real-memory access or weak-memory implementation proof; standard library only. All input/output containers in this task are built-in Python dict/list values; tuples and custom container classes are outside this exact interface.

Implement priority_inheritance(snapshots), a pure fixed-point analyzer for declared fixed-priority ownership/wait graphs. snapshots is a list of0..20 complete independent snapshots, each exactly {base,owners,waits}. base maps0..32 task IDs to integer priorities0..255, with HIGHER numbers more urgent in this mathematical model; integers exclude bool. owners maps0..32 lock IDs to an existing owner task ID or None. waits maps a subset of task IDs to one lock each; every waited-on lock is owned by a DIFFERENT existing task. All referenced tasks/locks exist. Task and lock IDs are case-sensitive1..24-character ASCII [A-Za-z0-9_-] strings. One task can own multiple locks and many tasks can wait on one lock; dependency cycles are allowed as graph inputs. Return one dictionary per snapshot mapping EVERY task to the LEAST fixed point E[t]=max(base[t], E[w] for each w waiting on a lock owned by t). Derive priorities from that snapshot's base graph rather than carrying old donations forward. This must propagate urgency through blocked-owner chains, combine donors across held locks, and remove obsolete donations while retaining a remaining equal/higher donor. Empty snapshots returns[]; an empty graph snapshot yields{}. Output integer types, keys and values are exact. Do not mutate inputs, retain state across calls or alias earlier output snapshots. No outside-domain validation required; standard library only. This computes a specified donation rule, not a Linux scheduler simulation, a claim that every input graph is admitted by kernel lock APIs, FIFO/fairness, runnable status, deadline guarantees or deadlock recovery. All input/output containers in this task are built-in Python dict/list values; tuples and custom container classes are outside this exact interface.
